declared_flips.note: These Wave-0 nodes freeze facts the change DECLARES will change. They are correct Wave-0 truth and must not be weakened now; the wave named below owns the revision, under revision_rule, with a recorded baseline rerun. Any Wave-0 node NOT listed here encodes a preserved surface: an unexplained difference stops the wave.

helpers.rule: When a wave moves one of these owners the harness re-points its spy/stub to the new owner module. The fixtures MUST replay unchanged. Regenerating a trace fixture because a spy target moved destroys the only pre-move ordered evidence and is prohibited.
Wave 3 moves the canonical owner to cache_workflow.py and keeps the pipeline re-export exact; re-point the patches, keep the receipt bytes equal.
Wave 4 replaces the handler with src.training.reporting.CompletedStepReporter; re-point the call site, keep every row byte and lifecycle counter equal.
Wave 1 deletes the private helper in favour of TokenSequence.causal_logits_positions(); re-point the call, keep the selected positions and the empty/absent-atom results equal.

Wave 1 gives the schema identity its canonical owner (src.training.micro_steps.supervised_micro_step_schema_identity) and Wave 3 moves the determinant projection to cache_contract.py. The identity payload itself is pure field data - class name, frozen flag, field names/annotations/defaults - and MUST stay exactly equal across every wave.

Wave 2 moves the bounded rank-report transport to src/training/control_plane.py. This suite must re-point its imports to the new owner in the same commit; every assertion - frame width, magic, payload bound, control timeout, eight-rank ordering, and error convergence - MUST replay unchanged. A repoint is never grounds to change an expected value, and an unresolved import here is a collection error, not a skip.

harness_seam_repoints.note: These characterization helpers spy on or stub module attributes of src.training.pipeline (and one private trainer helper). When a wave moves an owner, the harness re-points to the new owner and the frozen fixture must replay UNCHANGED. A moved spy target is never a reason to regenerate a fixture.

launch_bearing_actions.note: These are NOT test commands and are deliberately absent from this manifest. Each requires a fresh user authorization packet bound to the exact wave commit, full argv, absent targets, and numeric resource bounds; planning or implementation approval is not launch authority.

packet_freezes: one build-capable `conda run -n ms python -m src.prepare_train_cache ...` argv and its absent receipt path
one `--require-all-hit` argv with a distinct absent receipt path and no materialization authority
world_size=2, at most two GPUs, one planned/applied optimizer step
config-derived ceilings for forwards, collectives, wall time, CPU RSS, GPU high-water, artifact bytes, free disk

pass_rule: A gate PASSES when the observed failure node set equals that command's expected_red_nodes union the declared_flips entries whose flips_at_wave is less than or equal to the gate's wave and whose revision has not yet landed. Any other failure, any expected-RED node that unexpectedly passes, and any SKIPPED characterization node block the wave: a skip is reported, never counted as executed coverage.
revision_rule: Any added or changed command, node path, environment selector, or expected-RED entry requires an explicit manifest revision plus a recorded baseline rerun. Wave gates invoke IDs; they never expand the suite ad hoc.

runtime.note: No pytest-randomly / pytest-xdist / pytest-timeout plugin is installed, so collection order is deterministic and timeout_seconds is a wall-clock stop bound for the invoking operator, not a pytest option.
